Hallmarking of gold ornaments
†*341. SHRIMATI SAVITA
SHARDA:Will the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION  be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal for hallmarking of gold ornaments
in view of heavy loss to consumers as a
result of mixing of other metals in  gold
ornaments;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, by when a final decision is
likely to be taken in  this regard?
Telephone directory for Delhi and
Mumbai
*342. SHRI DINESH TRIVEDI:
SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY   be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that in spite of a
large number of changes in the telephone
numbers in Mumbai, Delhi and all metros
and the directive of the Hon'ble Supreme
Court of India to make directories available
to the telephone subscribers annually, the
main  telephone directories for Delhi and
Mumbai have not been published since
1999 and 2000 respectively;
(b) what steps MTNL has taken to
ensure that telephone directories  are made
available to the subscribers of Delhi and
Mumbai in time on a regular basis; and
(c) whether Government have examined
the feasibility of bringing out the directories
by  fixed dates?
Increase in turnover of IT industry
†*343. SHRI RAJIV RANJAN
SINGH 'LALAN':
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that overall
turnover of the information technology
industry is constantly increasing;
(b) if so, the total turnover of this
industry in the country and abroad during
the year 2002-03; and
(c) to what extent it is higher in
comparison to the last year?

Production of sugar
*344. SHRIMATI JAMANA DEVI
BARUPAL:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD  AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION  be pleased to state:
(a) whether sugar season showed an
excess of sugar production in 2002-03
(October-September);
(b) if so, what was the total sugar
production in 2002-03;
(c) whether in the sugar season of
2003-04, the assessment up-till nine
months show that the 200 lakh tonnes mark
has been crossed;
(d) if so, whether the excess production
of sugar would create a problem in the
country;
(e) whether Government are considering
to export more and more sugar during this
year;
(f) if so, the efforts being made; and
(g) whether more export orders have
been obtained?
Unspent money with missions
*345. SHRI RAVULA
CHANDRA  SEKAR  REDDY: Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Comptroller and
Auditor General of India in its latest report
on India's diplomatic missions abroad has
criticised the practice of missions keeping
unspent money for long with them;
(b) the number of missions which have
been found doing so; and
(c) what steps have been taken by
Government to ensure that this practice is
discontinued?
China's  refusal  to  recognise
Arunachal Pradesh as Indian
territory
*346. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE:
SHRI MANOJ
BHATTACHARYA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Chinese Government has
refused to recognise Arunachal Pradesh as
part of India;
(b) if so, the details thereof including
the context in which the refusal was
communicated to India;
(c) Government's reaction thereto;
(d) whether Government's viewpoint
has been communicated to the Chinese
Government; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Disparity in minimum wage
*347. DR. ABRAR AHMED:
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
Will the Minister of LABOUR be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any disparity in
rates of minimum wage in various regions
of the country; if so, the details thereof;
(b) the reasons for variation from region
to region; and
(c) the steps being taken to bring in
regional uniformity in this regard?
Draft hardware policy

Tackling of economic crimes by CBI
2543. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
DR. M.N. DAS:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the CBI has set up
Economic Intelligence Wing to tackle the
growing menace of economic crimes in
India;
(b) whether this wing represents Senior
Officials of the Reserve Bank of India, some
CBI officers of the Dy. Inspector General
rank in probing Economic Offences in the
country;
(c) if so, what would be the main task,
power and functions of this wing;
(d) to what extent it would help to check
the economic offenders; and
(e) whether any report would be
submitted to Government from time to
time?
Condition of ARIs in Karnataka
2544. SHRI M.V. RAJASEKHARAN:
DR. VIJAY MALLYA:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND
RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that the condition of traditional
rural and cottage industries has been
deteriorating and are on the verge of closure
especially in Karnataka;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
improve their condition and the extent to
which Government have succeeded in
improving the situation?
Reduction in interest rate of loan
2545. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
reduce the interest rate on loans given for
starting agro and rural industries and
whether appropriate authorities would be
recommended suitably in this regard;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Funds allocated for PMRY in U.P.
†2546. DR. AKHTAR HASAN RIZVI:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether any funds have been

Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana in the year

(b) if so, the details thereof?
Disbursement under PMRY in
Andhra Pradesh
2547. DR. DASARI NARAYANA
RAO: Will the Minister of AGRO AND
RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a
huge gap in bank-wise number of persons
recommended and actual disbursement
made by the banks under the PMRY in the
State of Andhra Pradesh;
(b) if so, the details thereof for the last
three years, year-wise and bank-wise;
(c) the reasons for such huge gaps; and
(d) the remedial measures being taken
by Government in this regard?
Promotion of KVIC
†2548. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are keeping in
view the factors like modern technique and
modern fashion for promoting Khadi and
Village Industries;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Modernisation of Khadi textiles
2549. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND
RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the steps Government have taken to
improve and modernise Khadi Textiles for
better acceptability and popularity;
(b) whether it is a fact that Government
have signed an MoU with the Textiles
Committee to make available laboratories
for quality testing and certification of khadi
products; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Expansion of oil production industries
†2550. SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
SHRI LAJPAT RAI:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND
RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether any scheme has been
formulated by Government for the
development and expansion of the oil
production industry at the rural level by
crushing the oilseeds produced in the
country;
(b) if so, the outline of the scheme and
the assessment made by Government
regarding the number of people who earn
at present their livelihood through this
industry throughout the country;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
Multinational Companies have already
entered in this industry; and
(d) if so, the names of such MNCs?
Setting up of rural industries
2551. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will
the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal to set up door-to-door industries
in the rural areas of the country on the
pattern of Japan;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
